string-array.name: changelog_51
string-array.item: Boarding wirelessly: if a VPN on yer phone keeps myCar off the ship\'s Wi-Fi, myCar now says so within seconds, on Home and in its notification, and tells ye how to set it right.
Apps that won\'t let myCar aboard, such as ABRP, now say why in plain words, get a red X and no longer set sail by themselves.

string-array.name: changelog_50
string-array.item: New Jolly Roger flag on the mast, above the ship\'s parrot: one tap does what ye choose: hail a mate, parley with an AI, run something in Home Assistant (a scene, a light, the gate), set a course for a port, give the parrot an order or board an app. Hold it to change it, aboard or on the phone in Rigging > Helm. Don\'t need it? Strike it there and the mast is as it was.

A call under way is now a wee bubble bobbing over every screen until it ends, with the photo of who ye\'re talking to, how long it has lasted and a red button to hang up. Tap it for the Phone; hold it and drag it anywhere, and it drops anchor there for the next calls too.

Spotify Web: a button on the cover of the shanty box beside the chart hoists video covers: shanties with a Canvas play their short looping video in place of the cover, until ye tap it again (also in Rigging). If no video shows, open Spotify\'s Now playing view once and pick its Canvas view.
The split screens (chart and shanties, an app beside the chart, the decks) are now soft rounded panels riding above the wallpaper.

Boarding wirelessly: a home Wi-Fi with addresses like the ship\'s no longer holds it in port for minutes, myCar starts over at once when the ship\'s wireless adapter restarts, and it hails the adapter again a few seconds after its Bluetooth comes aboard.
New \"Keep the ship\'s radio till the phone strikes up\": with the sound through myCar, the ship stays on its own radio (DAB+, FM) until something plays on the phone.

After ye switch to the ship\'s radio, a chart\'s voice, a web page or the parrot no longer make off with it, and spoken turns, answers and the parrot\'s listening beep lower the radio and hand it back, as Android Auto does.

With the sound through myCar, when the ship takes the speakers for a moment (its own voice, an announcement), the phone\'s shanties pause and strike up again afterwards instead of playing to nobody aboard.
Spotify Web sets sail by itself at the start of a voyage, even when the ship\'s radio presses Play again while the page is still loading.

When the phone\'s voice can\'t speak, myCar shows the answer and brings the shanties back within seconds, and on the phone myCar\'s Rigging > Parrot tells ye which voice is missing. The big voice model comes aboard only on longer voyages, and only when the phone has the memory to hold it.
If Home Assistant\'s voice assistant has lost its conversation agent, myCar asks one that\'s still afloat, or tells ye what to patch up.
Screen sharing keeps the phone\'s screen lit, turns the phone the way the ship\'s picture is, keeps the shanties playing aboard, and tells ye how to get back aboard myCar.

On the cable: Home tells ye what to check when the phone charges but no ship answers the hail (on GrapheneOS, the USB-C port setting), and the first fit-out explains what each Sound aboard choice means.
A ship with an upright screen gets an upright picture when it offers one, and Screen trim no longer says \"No vessel profile matched\".
A Waze modified with Morphe that won\'t let myCar aboard gets a red X, and the ship tells ye what to add to the patch.

From Gearslip: alerts from ship\'s apps on the ship\'s screen (Waze asks whether a hazard is still there), older Hyundais that ran aground at the start, spoken turns that come back when the voice didn\'t start, shanties that strike up again by themselves after the voyage put back on pause, Metrolist\'s Treasure button, AntennaPod\'s Next chapter o\' the yarn, and the name ye gave yer ship in Bluetooth.

Ships that kept their screen black with the shanties on Bluetooth (such as the Mitsubishi Mirage 2024) get it after 5 seconds, and at once when myCar knows them; Toyota head units that stalled before a wireless boarding get the answer they wait for; and for ships that need it, the phone\'s Bluetooth address can be written in Rigging > Boarding.
The voyage report says whether the ship switched off, went silent or lost its Wi-Fi under way.

string-array.name: changelog_49
string-array.item: Xonos inside myCar now sails with the engine of Xonos 0.1.55: an artist opens without hauling all its songs aboard first (they come aboard when ye open \"Every shanty\"), and the ship\'s menu waits for Music Assistant instead of showing empty holds.
With Music Assistant on yer phone, in the Xonos app: playing, skipping and picking a song wait up to a minute while it hoists sail again, instead of crying it ain\'t connected.

Sturdier Xonos: a sound decoder that springs a leak is swapped out, the sign-in is renewed before it runs dry, and Spotify, left tied up in Music Assistant by a stream nobody hears any more, is cut loose when no other player uses it (with an admin account).
If the car is switched off while the network is down or during a call, Xonos no longer strikes up again on the phone\'s speaker when the network returns or the call ends.
After ye pick an album or a playlist aboard, the player no longer keeps showing its name instead of the shanty that\'s playing. Shanties without a cover now fly Xonos\'s song icon.

string-array.name: changelog_48
string-array.item: Autoplay no longer strikes up the shanties on the phone\'s speaker, down in yer pocket, when the ship\'s Bluetooth music ain\'t aboard yet: it waits up to a minute, and a pause or a song ye pick meanwhile stays.

string-array.name: changelog_47
string-array.item: The chart no longer goes black and loses its position when the ship\'s Wi-Fi drops and comes back mid-voyage, or when ye board while myCar is left open on the locked phone. Steady as she goes!
With pirate speak, the voice and the phone numbers follow yer phone\'s home port again.

string-array.name: changelog_46
string-array.item: Fixed a crash that sank myCar and ended the voyage: it struck after a tap in Plancia\'s page, then a turn to the chart or the fleet, the Plancia app taking its place, or a change of paint.
Pirate speak: in Rigging > Tongue, every text of myCar in pirate terms, in yer own tongue. We chart our own course and bow to no crown.
A fresh moving wallpaper, myCar · Rebel: the waves, and a pirate ship that rides out every storm, skull and crossbones flying high.
If myCar ever closes by itself, the next start writes in the ship\'s log why Android scuttled it (a crash, memory, not responding), so the hole can be patched.
The parrot\'s voice models come aboard one at a time, never once the voyage is over, and before the first command only with memory to spare in the hold.
Wee shanty box: on small screens it sets out clear of the chart\'s buttons, let go under them it drifts just clear, and the chart\'s faded buttons no longer steal taps meant for the chart.
Verses: every shanty starts from its first line, and a live version of another shanty no longer smuggles in its words.
Spotify and the other shanty services: \"play …\" waits up to 25 seconds for the page, and a Play still waiting doesn\'t start once you\'ve switched shanties.

Choosing the ship\'s radio stops a video or a radio playing in Cinema or the browser, and they don\'t start again by themselves. Autoplay strikes up the shanties only once the sound has a course to the ship.

Parrot: \"next\", \"pause\" or \"stop\" inside a longer question no longer change the shanty; \"don\'t send\" and \"cancel\" are heard while you answer a message; a pause right before another shanty command no longer cancels it.
Fresh plunder waits for a call to end, and during a call the decks beside the chart and their menu stay below the call\'s bar.
Changing myCar\'s tongue mid-voyage switches the helm at once; on Android 12 and 13, opening myCar mid-voyage gives the chart its position back.
